nodes.title: The effective lift: computing formal solutions
nodes.statement: liftSolve takes a regular NTQ system U over F(A) (a regular standard quadratic equation is the one-level case) and an equation V(X, Y, A) = 1 with the promise that V is compatible with U, and searches the words Y(X) over X ∪ A in a fixed enumeration, testing V(X, Y(X)) = 1 in F_{R(U)} with the word-problem decider of FG10/frf-basic-algorithms (F_{R(U)} is fully residually free); it returns the first Y found. With an inequation W, it also tests W(X, Y(X)) ≠ 1.
hypotheses: Promise: V (and V ∧ W ≠ 1) compatible with the regular NTQ system U.
proofSteps: Enumerate candidate tuples of words; decide the equations in F_{R(U)} by FG10's word problem; stop at the first success.
acceptance: For U = [x₁,y₁][x₂,y₂] and V = ([z, x₁] = 1 ∧ z ≠ 1), liftSolve returns z = x₁ (or another nontrivial power of the root of x₁ in F_{R(U)}).

nodes.title: Correctness, computability and termination of the effective lift
nodes.statement: liftSolve is partial recursive; on every input (U, V, W) in the promised class (U regular NTQ, V ∧ W ≠ 1 compatible with U) it halts, and its output Y satisfies V(X, Y) = 1 and W(X, Y) ≠ 1 in F_{R(U)}, i.e. it is a complete-lift witness. Termination is FG11/ift-regular-ntq (a solution exists, so the enumeration reaches it); correctness of the returned answer is the word-problem test; no negative answer is produced.
proofSteps: Combine FG11/ift-regular-ntq (existence), FG10/frf-basic-algorithms-correct (the word-problem test is correct and total on F_{R(U)}), and enumeration of words.
acceptance: On U = [x₁,y₁][x₂,y₂], V = (z = x₁ y₁), the output is z = x₁ y₁.

nodes.title: Lifts under substitution and changes of coordinates
nodes.statement: (1) If σ is a G-automorphism of G[X] (a change of coordinates) and T(X, Y) = 1 admits a (complete) S-lift, then T(σX, Y) = 1 admits a (complete) S^σ-lift, where S^σ is the transformed system, and the formal solutions correspond under the induced isomorphism of coordinate groups. (2) If T(X, Y) = 1 admits an S-lift Y(X) and T′(X, Y, Z) = 1 admits an (S ∪ T)-lift Z(X, Y), then T ∧ T′ admits an S-lift (X, Y(X), Z(X, Y(X))) when G_{R(S∪T)} retracts onto G_{R(S)}. (3) In particular regularity and the conclusions of FG11/ift-regular-quadratic are invariant under the reduction to standard form of FG6/quadratic-standard-form, so the theorem applies to every quadratic equation whose standard form is regular.
proofSteps: (1) FG5/points-and-coordinate-changes; (2) compose the retractions of FG11/lift-characterisation (2); (3) apply (1) to the automorphism of FG6/quadratic-standard-form.
acceptance: The non-standard equation x y x⁻¹ y⁻¹ z w z⁻¹ w⁻¹ = 1 has a regular standard form and inherits the implicit function theorem.

gaps.title: Makanin's minimal-solution bound read only through secondary accounts
gaps.detail: FG7/minimal-solution-bound is stated as in Makanin's work, but Makanin's papers (Izv. 1982 and 1984) were not read: the Math-Net.ru pages did not respond. The proof sketch follows the account of Makanin's process in IFT §5 (which cites Makanin and Razborov for the exponent-of-periodicity bound, Lemmas 30–31 citing their earlier papers) and VAR-II §§1–3; RECOMP Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 give an independent route with rational constraints. A follow-up must read the exponent-of-periodicity bound (Bulitko's lemma) and the termination argument of Makanin's process at declaration level, or plan the RECOMP route, before the solver nodes are formalised.

gaps.title: Equations over a represented limit group: the elimination process over NTQ groups
gaps.detail: The specification requires the prerequisite proof cited by KM06 Theorem 32 to be resolved or replaced by a proved route. KM06 (J. Algebra 302, 2006) could not be read (the publisher refused automated access). The available sources give: JSJ Theorem 3.23 (decidability of the Diophantine problem in finitely generated fully residually free groups, cited from another paper of Kharlampovich–Myasnikov), JSJ Theorem 14.1 (complete Hom(G, N)-diagrams into NTQ groups, ‘proved in [41]’ and only sketched via the elimination process over groups with free regular Lyndon length functions, JSJ §§12–13), and Theorems 12.6–12.7 (free regular length functions on NTQ groups, proved in JSJ §12). A follow-up must read the elimination process over NTQ groups (JSJ [41] and KM06 Theorem 32) at declaration level and plan its generalised equations over infinite words, or adopt another proved route; until then FG10/equations-over-limit-groups rests on this gap and nothing downstream may use it as an oracle.
